lead: Rhode Island plumbing deals with old housing, coastal storms and cold winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across the state.
risk: aging pipes in older homes, coastal flooding and frozen pipes
risk_short: old pipes, coastal flooding and frozen pipes
why: Rhode Island has a lot of older housing, including triple-deckers in Providence and Pawtucket with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Lead service lines remain in some older homes.
Coastal storms and hurricanes flood low areas, and winters freeze pipes. Many homes heat with oil or gas boilers. The Department of Labor and Training licenses plumbers.
tips: Shut off the main valve before a storm evacuation.
Ask your utility about your service line.
areas: Calls come from Providence, Warwick, Cranston, Pawtucket, East Providence, Newport and South County.

faq.q: Who licenses plumbers in Rhode Island?
faq.a: The Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training licenses plumbers. Check the license before work starts.
